title: Refract verifier verdict
description: ai/runs/<run_id>/verdict.json (mode acceptance) or verdict-refute.json (mode refute) — the independent judge's record. The verifier (.claude/agents/verifier.md) ends its final message with this JSON; the SubagentStop hook persist-verdict.sh extracts it, validates it against this schema AND the rules a schema cannot state (below), stamps `signer`, `authors` and `scope`, and writes the file. Malformed output, a kept finding without proof, or a PASS the evidence does not support makes the hook exit 2 and the verifier redo the work. Rules enforced in .claude/scripts/refract_records.py: acceptance mode lists every criterion of the locked acceptance.json exactly once; a PASS criterion carries exit_code 0 and oracle `expresses-clause`; a regression criterion's PASS cites a red_run that exists verbatim in .claude/evidence/test-runs.jsonl; refute mode's confirmed findings carry file, line and proof, unconfirmed ones the settling probe, refuted ones the failed gate; `verdict` is derived — FAIL when any criterion FAILs or any confirmed IMPORTANT finding stands, CONCERNS when anything is UNVERIFIED or unconfirmed at IMPORTANT, PASS otherwise. PRE-EXISTING never blocks. Vocabulary: PASS ≡ READY (security's GO), CONCERNS ≡ GO-UNVERIFIED, FAIL ≡ NOT-READY (NO-GO).

contract.description: acceptance mode: the contract graded — ai/runs/<run_id>/acceptance.json, or the plan file for a plan-<id> run.

command.description: What the verifier ran at HEAD.

oracle.description: Does the test's assertion state the EARS clause (expresses-clause), something correlated with it (proxy), or nothing (absent)? Only expresses-clause can PASS.

note.description: The assertion line read (file:line) and why it does or does not express the clause; for a FAIL, the failing output.

red_run.description: regression criteria: the RED record of the test before the fix, copied from .claude/evidence/test-runs.jsonl.

id.description: The candidate's id, or <reviews file>#F-n when it came from a persisted review.

gate.description: refuted: the gate that failed; unconfirmed: the gate left unresolved.

probe.description: unconfirmed: the exact probe that would settle it.
